Area.evidence_source: Suicidal thoughts following sexual violence are based on a strong self-destructive force which shapes survivors' existence, appearing in risk behaviour and indifference towards own life and health. The stigma associated with men showing their emotions must be eliminated. They must be able to disclose their traumatic experiences. Furthermore, the expertise of healthcare practitioners could be improved by increased knowledge and a deeper understanding of their client0 s personal traumas. This could enable them to provide appropriate trauma-specific support to male sexual violence survivors who have suicidal ideas, thereby increasing the chance of disclosure and healing, as well as of reporting the violence which can prevent perpetrators in violating against boys and men. Public policies and service provisions need to be improved to meet the needs of men who have been sexually violated against.
